Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 10, verse 31:

﴿Qul man yarzuqukum minas-sama'i wal-ard﴾: Say (O Prophet): Who provides you sustenance from the heavens and the earth? (Meaning: by sending down rain from the sky and producing vegetation from the earth.) Or the meaning may be: who among the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth provides you sustenance?

﴿Amman yamliku's-sam'a wal-absar﴾: Or, who is it that has complete control over your hearing and sight? That is, who is able to make you hear and see? Whose power is it that can make you hear whatever word one wishes to convey and see whatever thing one wishes to show? Or the meaning is: who gave you the power of hearing and seeing, and who created hearing and sight and kept them in proper order? Or the meaning is: despite the abundance of accidents and diseases, who preserves your hearing and sight and protects them from being affected?

﴿Wa man yukhriju'l-hayya minal-mayyiti wa yukhriju'l-mayyita minal-hayy﴾: And who brings the living out of the dead, such as a living creature from a lifeless drop of semen or an egg, and brings the drop of semen or the egg out of the living creature?

﴿Wa man yudabbiru'l-amr﴾: And who manages all affairs and knows the outcomes and consequences of all matters?

﴿Fa-sayaqulunallah﴾: Then they will say: "Allah." That is, they will not be able to attribute these matters to the partners they have invented.

﴿Fa-qul afala tattaqun﴾: Then say to them: Why, then, do you not guard yourselves against shirk? That is, why do you not fear associating helpless, powerless creatures with Allah, the Mighty and Capable, in worship? Do you not fear the punishment of Allah?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verses 32–33:

﴿Then that is Allah, your true Lord.﴾ That is Allah, the One who alone is entitled to be worshipped, who is your true Lord, whose lordship is established both by innate awareness (wijdan) and by proof. Since it is He who created you, provided you with sustenance, and arranged all your affairs, then who else could be your Lord? He is the Truth. His existence is beyond doubt, and His ownership is beyond suspicion.

﴿So what is there after the truth but error?﴾ The question is rhetorical: after the truth there is nothing but error. Therefore, whoever abandons the truth and associates others with Allah in worship is in error.

﴿Then how are you turned away?﴾ That is, how are you being turned away from the truth towards falsehood?
