Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 34:

Say: "Is there any of your (supposed) partners who originates creation and then repeats it?" That is: the One who begins the creation is the one who, after reducing it to non-existence, brings it back again. Who besides Him can do this?

Say: "It is Allah who originates creation and then repeats it" (that is, after its annihilation, just as it was before).

"Then how are you turned away?" That is: how do you turn from the worship of Allah to the worship of others, from truth to falsehood? The demand of the proof is the oneness of the object of worship and the negation of association (shirk).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 35:

Say: "Is there any among your (supposed) partners who guides to the truth?" (Say, asking them) whether among your supposed partners there is one who guides to the truth, by establishing proofs, by sending messengers, by granting the capacity for sound reflection, and by creating the means of guidance.

Say: "It is Allah who guides to the truth." Say (yourself): Allah alone guides to the truth; no one else has the power to do so.

"Then is one who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or one who cannot find the way unless he is guided?" That is: when Allah guides him, he can be guided himself and can guide others too; without Allah's guidance he can do nothing. This is the condition of the great (supposed) partners of the polytheists. Christ, Ezra and the angels (whom the polytheists declare to be partners in the worship of Allah) themselves depend on Allah both for being guided and for guiding others. Some commentators have written that guidance (hidayah) means moving from one place to another. This verse shows the helplessness of idols: they cannot move themselves; others lift them and move them. How then can they deserve to be worshipped?

"What is the matter with you? How do you judge?" So (O disbelievers!) what has happened to you, that you make a judgment whose falsehood is entirely evident?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 36:

And most of them follow nothing but conjecture. Indeed, conjecture does not avail against the truth in the least. Most of them, in their beliefs, follow only assumption. No rational proof and no transmitted evidence supports their assumptions. They have established nothing but futile fancies and faulty analogies. Analogizing the Unseen to the Seen, and the Creator to the created, on the basis of some imaginary point of commonality, is nothing more than a baseless conjecture.

By "most" is meant either all the disbelievers (since all of them are superstitious, and there is no reasonable proof for shirk in the possession of anyone), or it refers to those who claim discernment and reflection and who reject blind imitation (since, when people of intellect and discernment take illusion for understanding and conjecture for certainty, the superstition of the ordinary disbelievers is all the more evident; they do not even claim to possess intellect).

﴿Indeed, conjecture does not avail against the truth in the least.﴾ Mere intellectual hair-splitting (tak bandi) is utterly powerless against knowledge and the belief in truth. It cannot benefit anyone, nor can any portion of the truth be obtained through it.

From this verse it becomes clear that in matters of creed, mere intellectual hair-splitting and the blind imitation of others are not permissible; rather, it is necessary to acquire certain knowledge in the light of rational and transmitted proofs.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.﴾ Their actions are fully known to Allah. This contains a warning for those who turn away from rational and transmitted proofs and follow illusion and imitation.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 37:

وما کان ھذا القرآن ان یفترٰی من دون اللہ اور یہ قرآن ایسا نہیں کہ اللہ کی طرف سے نازل ہوئے بغیر ازخود اس کو بنا لیا جائے اور ان کی طرف اس کی نسبت کردی جائے۔

Translation: "And this Qur'an could not have been invented apart from Allah." And this Qur'an is not such that it could be fabricated by itself without being sent down from Allah, and then attributed to Him.

ولکن تصدیق الذی بین یدیہ بلکہ یہ تو ان کتابوں کی تصدیق کرنے والا ہے جو اس سے پہلے نازل ہوچکی ہیں۔

Translation: "But it is a confirmation of that which is before it." Rather, it is a confirmer of the books that were sent down before it.

الَّذِیْ بَیْنَ یَدَیْہِ سے مراد یا رسول اللہ (ﷺ) کی ذات مبارک ہے ‘ یا گزشتہ کتب الٰہیہ (ترجمہ میں یہی بیان کیا ہے) یا قیامت ‘ یا بعثت نبوی جس کی خبر سابق کتابوں میں دے دی گئی تھی۔

Translation: By "that which is before it" (alladhi bayna yadayhi) is meant either the blessed person of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), or the previous divine books (as stated in the translation), or the Resurrection, or the prophethood of the Prophet (ﷺ), the news of which had been given in the earlier scriptures.

و تفصیل الکتب لاریب فیہ من رب العٰلمین۔ اور احکام ضروریہ (الٰہیہ) کی تفصیل بیان کرنے والا ہے ‘

Translation: "And an elaboration of the Book, there is no doubt in it, from the Lord of the worlds." And it is an elaboration of the essential (divine) rulings,

اس میں کوئی بات شک (و شبہ) کی نہیں کہ یہ رب العالمین کی طرف سے ہے۔

Translation: there is no doubt whatsoever that it is from the Lord of the worlds.

تفصیل الکتاب (احکام ضروریہ کی تفصیل) یعنی لوح محفوظ میں اللہ کے احکام ‘ فرائض اور حلال و حرام کی تشریح ہے۔ اس کا بیان یہ قرآن ہے۔ لاَ رَیْبَ فِیْہِ یعنی اس میں کوئی بات شک کے قابل نہیں کیونکہ یہ گزشتہ آسمانی کتابوں کے بالکل موافق ہے۔

Translation: Tafsil al-Kitab (the elaboration of the essential rulings), that is, the explanation of Allah's commands, obligations, and what is lawful and unlawful in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). Its exposition is this Qur'an. La rayba fihi (there is no doubt in it) means that it contains nothing open to doubt, because it is completely in accord with the earlier heavenly books.

سابق آیت میں دماغی تک بندیوں کے اتباع کی ممانعت کی گئی ہے۔ اس آیت میں واجب الاتباع کتاب کا ذکر ہے اور تنبیہ ہے کہ اس قرآن کا اتباع کیا جائے۔ اس کا اتباع لازم ہے۔

Translation: In the previous verse, following mere mental conjectures was prohibited. In this verse, the Book that must be followed is mentioned, and there is a warning that this Qur'an should be followed. Following it is obligatory.

Do they say, "He has invented it"? Say: "Then bring a surah like it." That is: if I have composed it myself, then you too should bring one surah that is like it in eloquence, style and the strength of its meaning. After all, you too are Arabs, capable of speech, and masters of expression and style.

And call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful [in claiming that Muhammad (ﷺ) has composed it himself]. In this verse, the challenge is given to consider the words and meanings of the Qur'an and to call upon helpers for debate, so that it is said afterwards:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 10, verse 39:

﴿Nay, they denied that of which they had no knowledge and whose interpretation had not yet come to them.﴾ That is, their speech and their denial of the truth of the Qur'an are not based on any reflection or investigation. Rather, without knowing the reality of the Qur'an and without any reflection, merely upon hearing it, they refused to accept the Qur'an as the word of Allah. They had not yet even considered that this speech is beyond human power. The unseen news that the Qur'an has conveyed, the knowledge of the origin and the return, and the information about reward and punishment, have not yet reached their time of manifestation. It was incumbent upon them to ask the scholars of the earlier scriptures whether these matters that the Qur'an declares are also found in their books. Through such an inquiry, the truthfulness of the Qur'an would certainly have become clear to them. The inimitability of the Qur'an's wording, teaching and meanings can become manifest to those who reflect, think and investigate the sciences of the Qur'an. But they neither reflected upon the words of the Qur'an nor examined its meanings, and they immediately set about denying it.

﴿لَمَّا یَأتِھِمْ﴾ "Not yet has its interpretation come to them." Here, لَمَّا is a word of expectation, which gives hope that the inimitability of the Qur'an will become manifest. Thus, when they were repeatedly challenged to contest it, and they expended all their strength against the Qur'an and tested it, and their powers of opposition availed them nothing, then the Qur'an's inimitability became manifest to them. Similarly, the reports the Qur'an gave repeatedly came to light and were proved true, as in the words ﴿غُلِبَتِ الرُّوْمُ﴾ and so on, that the Romans were defeated but would soon prevail. Later, the Romans did indeed prevail over the Persians. Or as in ﴿تَبَّتْ یَدآ اَبِی لَھَبٍ وَّتَبَّ﴾, where the destruction of Abu Lahab was foretold, and it was fulfilled. After this experience, some people believed, and some remained disbelievers under the influence of enmity. The truth had become apparent even to the opponents; they had recognised its truthfulness. ﴿یَعْرِفُوْنَّہُ کَمَا یَعْرِفُوْنَ اَبْنَآءَھُمْ﴾ (They recognised it as they recognise their own sons.) In their hearts they too had become certain of the Qur'an's truth, but out of obstinacy they refused to accept it. ﴿وَجَحَدُوْا بِھَا وَاسْتَیْقَنَتْھَآ اَنْفُسُھُمْ﴾ (And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them.)

﴿کَذٰلِکَ کَذَّبَ الَّذِیْنَ مِنْ قَبْلِھِمْ﴾ Thus did those before them deny (the messengers and the divine books). That is, just as these people denied the Qur'an, so too the disbelievers before them denied their own divine books and the messengers sent by God.

﴿فَانْظُرْ کَیْفَ کَانَ عَاقِبَۃُ الظّٰلِمِیْنَ﴾ "Look, then, at how the end of the wrongdoers was." But look and see what the end of these wrongdoers was. This is a warning to the deniers of the Qur'an that if they do not desist, their outcome will be the same as that of the deniers before them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 10, verse 40:

Wa minhum man yu'minu bih: "And among them are some who believe in it" (those among these deniers who, after reflection, have faith in the truth of the Quran in their hearts). Or the meaning may be that when the truth of the Quran becomes clear to them in the future, some of them will believe and repent of disbelief. The word "lamma" (when/as yet not) gave the expectation of future belief; this sentence explicitly states that the expectation will be fulfilled.

Wa minhum man la yu'minu bih: "And among them are some who will never believe in it." The reason for their not believing is either their extreme foolishness, or that it has been written in advance in destiny that they will die in disbelief, and therefore they will not believe.

Wa rabbuka a'lamu bil-mufsidin: "And your Lord knows the corrupters well." That is, He is well aware of those who persist stubbornly and act with hostility.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 41:

﴿And if they deny you, say: "For me is my deed, and for you is your deed. You are free of what I do, and I am free of what you do."﴾

And (even after the proof has been established and they have been left without an answer), if they continue to deny you, then you (should declare your disassociation from them and) say: "My deed is for me, and your deed is for you" (I will be recompensed for my deed, and you will be recompensed for your deed). "You are apart from my deeds" (you will not be held accountable for my deeds; my actions cannot harm you, so do not cause me pain and do not fabricate accusations against me). "And I am free of your deeds; you will not be held to account for them by me."

I only tell you what I say for your own good. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The example of myself and of what Allah has sent me with is like that of a man who said to his people, 'I have seen the enemy army with my own eyes (beyond this mountain, and it will attack you in the last part of the night and destroy and slaughter you). I am warning you of this danger. Leave quickly and flee.'" Some of the people believed his words, took the opportunity, and set off during the night, and thus escaped the enemy's attack. But some of the people called the man a liar and remained in their place until morning. In the morning the enemy army attacked them, destroyed them all, and uprooted them completely. This is also the condition of those who accepted the teaching I brought, and affirmed me, or who denied me and did not accept the truth I brought. (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abu Musa.)

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: this verse has been abrogated (mansukh) by the verses of jihad, just as ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾ has been abrogated.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 42:

And among them are those who listen to you (outwardly). When you recite the Qur'an and speak of wisdom and the Shariah, they lend their ears outwardly, but they do not listen with the ears of the heart; they do not give their hearts any attention. They do not grasp the reality of wisdom and the Shariah because of the deficiency of their capacity. They are like full-bellied people who lend their ears, yet because they lack the power of hearing, they cannot hear.

﴿Then can you make the deaf hear, even though they do not understand?﴾ Can you make the deaf hear, when they are also without understanding? If a deaf person has understanding, he can grasp something from the circumstances and signs around him, but a deaf person without understanding cannot grasp anything. Therefore, just as you cannot make a deaf person without understanding hear, in the same way you cannot make hear those people who have lost the ability to listen with the ear of the heart and to comprehend through thought and insight.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 43:

وَمِنْهُم مَّن يَنظُرُ إِلَيْكَ — And among them are some who look at you with their eyes; they witness the signs of truth. The signs of the Prophet (ﷺ) are visible to them, but their hearts are blind. Because they lack inner sight, they do not affirm (they are, as it were, both blind and without insight).

أَفَأَنتَ تَهْدِي الْعُمْيَ وَلَوْ كَانُوا لَا يُبْصِرُونَ — "Will you then guide the blind, even though they cannot see?" That is, will you guide the blind even when, besides lacking sight, they also lack insight? For one who has lost his sight, if he also lacks insight, how can he see the way?

In the previous verse, the command was given to disassociate from the disbelievers who do not believe and to turn away from them. In these two sentences, the reason for that command is also stated, which also serves to console the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Those deaf who have no capacity to hear, and those blind who lack insight, you cannot make them hear, nor can you show them the way. Therefore, those whom I have deprived of faith, you cannot grant them the ability to believe.

Surah Yunus, verse 44: "Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people at all; but it is the people who wrong themselves."

In truth, Allah does not wrong people in the least; rather, people wrong their own souls. Because of the corruption of their natural faculties and the error of their choice and preference, they do not accept the path shown by Allah and by His Messenger (ﷺ) as correct.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The example of the guidance and the religious knowledge with which Allah has sent me is like rain falling upon a land. A portion of that land is good: it takes in the water and produces abundant vegetation and grass and fodder. Another portion is hard and rocky: it holds the water within itself, and Allah benefits people through it; they drink from it, give drink to others, and irrigate their crops. But there is another portion of land which is a barren plain: it neither holds the water nor produces any vegetation. Such is the condition of this religion. Some people understand the religion, and benefit from the teaching with which Allah has sent me; they learn it themselves and teach it to others. And some people pay no attention at all to the religion, do not even raise their heads to look at it, and do not accept the guidance with which I have been sent." (Agreed upon, from the hadith of Abu Musa.)

Some scholars have explained the meaning of the aforementioned verse as follows: that Allah should take away a person's sound senses and power of understanding, and deprive him of the instruments of reasoning (and then command him to follow guidance). Allah does not commit such injustice. Thus this verse establishes that man has been given the power of acquisition (kasb, i.e., action) and the power of choice; Allah has not taken away his capacity of choice. (The power to distinguish good from bad has been given even to ordinary people. If a person does not use this power, or uses it wrongly, the fault is his own.) By this, the view of the Jabriyya sect is refuted, those who regard man as powerless and compelled like a stone. It is also possible that in this verse there is a warning to those who deny prophethood and the Qur'an: that the punishment they will suffer on the Day of Judgment will not be an injustice upon them but pure justice. They themselves chose the causes of the punishment (as a result of which they will be punished).

On the Day He gathers them, it will seem as though they had not remained (in the world, or in the graves) except for an hour of a day. Because of the terror of the scene, they will regard the span of their worldly life, or of their stay in the grave, as no more than an hour.

They will recognise one another (يتعارفون بينهم): they will know each other as they did in the world, as though they had been separated only briefly and then gathered again, and no one will have forgotten anyone. Al-Baghawi has written: this mutual recognition will take place at the time of rising from the graves; then, because of the terror of the Day of Judgment, mutual acquaintance will cease. Some reports state that a person will recognise the one beside him but, out of awe and fear, will not speak to him.

﴿Those who denied the meeting with Allah have indeed lost﴾ (in the course of their mutual recognition, the deniers of the Resurrection will say that today they have been ruined, those who denied the Last Day and the going before Allah). Alternatively, this is a testimony from Allah (it is not the statement of the disbelievers): abandoning faith for disbelief and receiving Hell instead of Paradise is a great loss.

﴿And they were not of those who were guided﴾: and they were not people who would be guided, that is, who would use properly the instruments of knowledge and felicity that had been given to them. There is a sense of wonder in this clause.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 46:

﴿Whether We show you some of what We promise them, or We take you (in death), to Us is their return. Then Allah is Witness over what they do.﴾ Some of the punishment with which We threaten them, if We show you a part of it (you will see it), or (before its descent) We give you death; so they will return to Us (they cannot escape the punishment; We will show it to you in the Hereafter).

﴿Then Allah is Witness over what they do.﴾ That is, (as is well known) Allah is aware of all their deeds. The word "ittila'" (being informed) here means its result (the cause is mentioned in place of the effect). For this reason, witnessing has been made the result of return (i.e., the word "shahid" does not mean merely being informed, otherwise after their return on the Day of Resurrection, Allah's being informed of their deeds would have no meaning. Allah knows their deeds even in this world; He will not come to know them only after they return on the Day of Resurrection). However, if the meaning of "shahid" is taken as "one who punishes," the sense becomes correct: that all of them will return to Allah, and after their return Allah will punish them. The meaning is that Allah knows their deeds and on the Day of Resurrection will punish them on the basis of that knowledge. Some scholars said: the word "thumma" (then) is in the sense of "wa" (and); in that case the meaning is that Allah is aware of their deeds, and all of them will return to Allah. Thus both matters are stated separately in two independent sentences (there is no intended sequence of one matter before the other). Mujahid said: the part of the punishment which Allah showed to His Messenger (ﷺ) with his own eyes refers to the punishment of the day of Badr (the killing of the chiefs of disbelief and the lasting defeat of the disbelievers); the other kinds of punishment will occur after death.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 47:

Wa li-kulli ummatin rasulun: "And for every nation there is a messenger." A rasul (messenger) means one who is sent, a bearer of a command, one who calls to Islam.

Fa-idha ja'a rasuluhum qudiya baynahum bil-qisti wa hum la yuzlamun: "So when their messenger comes, judgement is passed between them with justice, and they are not wronged." That is, after the messenger (ﷺ) had come to them and conveyed the commands, and they denied the messenger (ﷺ), then judgement was passed on them with justice, and they were not wronged.

That is, when the messenger (ﷺ) presented the miracles and, even after that, they did not accept and declared the messenger (ﷺ) a liar, then Allah passed judgement with justice between the messenger (ﷺ) and his community. He destroyed those who denied, and He preserved the believers and the messenger (ﷺ). And this judgement of Ours was based on justice; We did not wrong them in punishing them.

Mujahid and Muqatil explained the meaning of the verses thus: every nation has had a messenger who was sent to that nation. When the Day of Judgement comes and every messenger comes to bear witness to the belief and disbelief of his nation, Allah will pass a just judgement, granting salvation to the believers and punishment to the disbelievers. A similar statement appears in another verse: "Wa ji'a bil-nabiyyina wal-shuhada'i wa qudiya baynahum" [And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and judgement will be passed between them]. In another place He said: "Fa kayfa idha ji'na min kulli ummatin bi-shahidin wa ji'na bika 'ala ha'ulai shahidan" [So how will it be when We bring a witness from every nation and bring you as a witness against these people?]

And they say, "When will this promise come to pass, if you are telling the truth?"

Verse 48 quotes them: "And they say, 'When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?'" That is, the disbelievers of Makkah say, "When will this punishment that you threaten us with come about? If you (Muhammad (ﷺ) and your companions) are truthful, then bring the promised punishment." The disbelievers of Makkah said this in mockery.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 49:

﴿Say: I possess not for myself any harm or benefit, except what Allah wills.﴾ (O Muhammad (ﷺ)!) Say: I do not even have control over the benefit or harm to my own self, except to the extent that Allah has willed me to have control. That is, I do not have the power to repel harm or to gain benefit, except the power that Allah has willed to give me. Or the meaning of ﴿illa ma sha'a Allah﴾ may be that whatever Allah wills is what happens; I have no power over my own benefit or harm.

﴿Likewise every nation has its term (ajal)﴾ (in the knowledge of Allah): the destruction of every nation has a fixed appointed time.

﴿So when their term comes, they cannot delay it by an hour, nor can they advance it.﴾ So when their appointed time arrives, then (at that time) they cannot withdraw even for an hour, nor can they move forward. Ajalahum means the appointed time for their punishment. Sa'ah means a short while. The meaning is: do not hasten for the punishment to come; it will soon arrive at its appointed time and the promise will be fulfilled.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 50:

Say: "Tell me: if His punishment comes upon you by night or by day, what is there in it that the guilty would hasten to have?"

Ma dha (مَا ذَا) here is an interrogative of wonder (istifham ta'ajjubi), meaning: it is astonishing that they seek to hasten a punishment, which is such an unpleasant thing. Hastening after something unpleasant is not appropriate.

The answer (jaza') to "in ataakum" (اِنْ اَتٰکُمْ, "if it comes upon you") is omitted, meaning: if the punishment comes upon you by night or by day, then at that time you will regret your haste in demanding it and will realise your error.

Baghawi has written: the disbelievers were eager for the punishment to come quickly. One of them said: "O Allah! If this is the truth, from You, then rain down stones on us from the sky, or bring upon us some other painful punishment." Allah, in response, says: for what punishment are they hastening? Punishment is something unpleasant for everyone.

I say: "Ma dha yasta'jilu" (مَا ذَا یَسْتَعْجِلُ) could be the answer (jaza') of the conditional. The meaning would then be: if Allah's punishment comes upon you, then in that situation, for what would you hasten? Would you ask for another punishment of the same kind, and choose to remain in punishment, or would you seek deliverance? Obviously, you would not be seekers of punishment.

Then, when it has come to pass, will you believe in it? That is, when that promised punishment comes upon you, you will believe in it, or in the one who gave the warning of the punishment (and you will be remorseful). Or the meaning is: when the punishment comes upon you, will you then also keep hurrying for it? Then, at that time, you will accept the punishment, or the one who informed of the punishment, when faith will be of no benefit.

(At the time of the punishment of the Hereafter, or when the rattle of death sounds, when you believe, then it will be said to you:) "Is it now (that you believe? Faith at such a time is of no avail)?"

"And you used to hasten it." Though (in denial and mockery) you were eager for the punishment to arrive quickly.
Then it will be said to those who did wrong: "Taste the everlasting punishment. You are being repaid only for what you used to earn."

They ask you, "Is it true?" Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true, and you cannot escape it." (Meaning: you cannot stop its coming or its truth from being realized, nor can you get away from it.) ʿAjaza ʿan al-shayʾ means that a person became unable to reach or overcome something, i.e., that thing eluded him or escaped him.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 54:

Wa law anna li-kulli nafsin ẓalamat mā fi'l-arḍi laftadat bihi. And (hypothetically) if every person who committed shirk were given, on the Day of Resurrection, all the treasures and hidden wealth that are on the earth, he would give it all in order to be freed from the punishment and to save himself. Mā fi'l-arḍi means the treasures of the earth and all the earthly things that are desired. Iftida' (ransom) and fida' have the same meaning: giving a substitute to escape punishment (sacrificing everything). Ẓulm here means shirk or injustice toward another person.

Wa asarrū al-nadāmata lammā ra'awu al-ʿadhāb. And when they see the punishment, they will feel regret in secret (within their hearts).

Abu ʿUbaydah said: Asarrū al-nadāmah means that at that time they will display their regret, because the Day of Resurrection will have no false display of patience or artificial endurance (the suffering will be so severe that no one will be able to show feigned patience or pretended forbearance). Some scholars said: the meaning of asarrū is that they will conceal their regret, that is, the powerful leaders will hide their regret from the weak followers under their influence, so that those who were misled through them will not blame them. Some scholars said that concealing regret means being unable to speak. When the unexpected and unsuspected punishment appears before them, they will be so astonished that they will not even be able to speak.

Some scholars said: the essence of a thing is called sirr. Like a secret, the essence of a thing is worth concealing and protecting; therefore the meaning of asrār here is pure regret.

Wa quḍiya baynahum bi'l-qisṭi wa hum lā yuẓlamūn. And judgment will be passed between them with justice, and they will not be wronged by being punished without fault. The meaning is that the oppressors will be punished for oppressing the oppressed. The matter between oppressor and oppressed will be decided with justice. The first quḍiya refers to the judgment between the prophets and their nations, and here quḍiya means punishing the polytheists for their shirk and having the oppressed obtain redress from the oppressors for their oppression, that is, punishing the oppressors.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 10, verse 55:

Alā inna lillāhi mā fis-samāwāti wal-arḍ: "Be certain that to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth." So He has the power to give reward and punishment (nothing in the whole of the earthly and heavenly creation lies outside His power).

Alā inna waʿda Allāhi ḥaqq: "Be certain that the promise of Allah is true." (The promise of reward and punishment made by Allah) is true. It cannot be broken; reward and punishment will certainly come to pass.

Wa lākinna aktharahum lā yaʿlamūn: "But most of them do not know" (because of a shortfall in understanding and comprehension). They know only the outward, worldly life.

He gives life and causes death; He is the One who gives life and causes death. Thus in the Hereafter He is able to give life and to cause death. His power cannot decline, nor can the one who accepts life and death change it.

And to Him you will be returned: (after death, rising from the graves) all of you will have to return to Him.

O people, there has come to you an admonition from your Lord: that is, the Qur'an has reached you through the tongue of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Qur'an is a call to awakening and a reminder, inviting to good deeds and restraining from evil, because these commands and prohibitions have been sent down by Allah, and Allah is Wise. What He commands you to do is certainly good and its outcome will be good; and what He forbids you from is certainly evil and its outcome will be evil. Good deeds are things to be desired, and evil deeds are things to be detested.

"And a healing for what is in the breasts": a healing medicine for the diseases of the hearts. The diseases of the heart mean false beliefs and attachment and dependence of the hearts on things other than Allah.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through a report from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that a man came into the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah! I have a pain in my chest." He said: "Recite the Qur'an." Allah has said (about the Qur'an): "And a healing for what is in the breasts" (Yunus 10:57). There is also a corroborating report of this hadith from Wathila ibn al-Asqa', which Bayhaqi narrated in Shu'ab al-Iman.

"And guidance": it is a guide. It shows the path to correct beliefs and thoughts, to Paradise, and to the degrees of nearness to Allah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: (On the Day of Resurrection) it will be said to the people who recited the Qur'an: "Recite and keep ascending, and recite with measured recitation (tartil) as you used to recite in the world, for your rank will be at the place where you reach at the last verse you recite." Related by Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i, from Abdullah ibn Amr.

"And a mercy for the believers": and for those who have faith, this is a mercy from Allah. The believers are the ones who benefit from it and who, by reciting it and acting upon its teaching, enjoy the mercy of Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 58:

Say: "By the grace of Allah and His mercy (O Muhammad ﷺ, say, in gratitude to Allah: by Allah's grace and mercy this admonition, healing, guidance and mercy has come to us; our deservingness has no part in it)."

Fa-bi-dhalika falyafrahu: then they should rejoice (at this grace and bounty of Allah and at the acquisition of the Quran). The placing of bi-dhalika first indicates that the thing worthy of rejoicing is the Quran and the grace and bounty of Allah; no other comfort or blessing of the world is a cause of joy.

Some scholars said that by the grace and mercy of Allah is meant only the sending down of the Quran. Mujahid and Qatadah said: the grace of Allah is faith, and the mercy of Allah is the Quran. Hadrat Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: the grace of Allah is faith, and the mercy of Allah is that Allah made us people of the Quran.

Abu al-Shaykh and others narrated on the authority of Hadrat Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: they should rejoice in Allah's grace, that is, the Quran, and in Allah's mercy, that is, that He made them among the people of the Quran.

Hadrat Ibn Umar said: the grace of Allah is Islam, and the mercy of Allah is that Allah made Islam beloved in our hearts.

Hadrat Khalid ibn Ma'dan said: the grace of Allah is Islam, and the mercy of Allah is the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It has also been said that the grace of Allah is faith and the mercy of Allah is the Sunnah.

Huwa khayrun mimma yajma'un: It (that is, the sending down of the Quran, or the grace and mercy of Allah) is better than what they are gathering (that is, the lowly worldly wealth which they accumulate).

Sayyid Qutb, Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation), on Surah 10, verse 59:

Say (O Muhammad (ﷺ)): "Tell me, the provision which Allah sent down for you, and you made from it some unlawful and some lawful."

"Anzala" (sent down) here means "created." The creation is described as being sent down because these things are produced through the upper means, that is, rain, and rain descends from above. Or it may be said that before the creation of the universe, Allah wrote the things He would create in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). Now the creation of provision follows the writing of the Tablet, so it is as if provision descends from the Preserved Tablet. By "provision" is meant crops or livestock that give milk. The word "lakum" (for you) shows that Allah had made these things lawful for you, but you (on your own authority) declared some of them lawful and some unlawful. The disbelievers had said: "These are cattle and tilled land, forbidden (hijr)." They also said: "What is in the bellies of these cattle is exclusively for our males and is forbidden to our females." They had also declared the bahirah, sa'ibah, wasilah and ham (various kinds of male camels) to be unlawful.

Say: "Has Allah given you permission (for this), or are you inventing lies against Allah?"

Say to them: Has Allah permitted you to make this lawful and unlawful (so that you are acting on His command), or are you fabricating falsehood against Allah, attributing this self-invented declaration of lawful and unlawful to Him? The meaning is that Allah has not permitted you to do so. You are yourselves slandering Allah and speaking a lie, claiming that Allah has commanded us to do this.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 10, verse 60:

﴿Those who invent lies against Allah, what do they think will happen to them on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ Do they think that on the Day of Resurrection they will not be punished for this fabrication against Allah? No! It will certainly happen. The vagueness of the word "ma" (what) in the verse indicates that this threat of punishment has been given by Allah to the disbelievers in a severe manner.

﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty towards mankind﴾. There is no doubt that Allah is very merciful to people. He bestowed the blessing of intellect, sent down books for guidance, and sent messengers.

﴿But most of them do not give thanks.﴾ But most people do not give thanks for this blessing. If they were giving thanks, they would act upon the command of reason and revelation and would not fabricate lies against Allah.

The meaning of the verse may also be that Allah is very merciful to His servants. The servants disobey, yet Allah does not immediately afflict them with punishment in this world; He keeps granting them respite (ḍheel, i.e. reprieve).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 61:

وما تکون فی شان وما تتلوا منہ من قرآن ولا تعملون من عمل الا کنا علیکم شہودًا اذ تفیضون فیہ اور (اے رسول (ﷺ)!) آپ (خواہ) کسی حال میں ہوں اور منجملہ ان احوال کے کہیں سے قرآن پڑھتے ہوں اور (اسی طرح، اے لوگو!) تم جو کام بھی کرتے ہو، ہم کو سب کی خبر رہتی ہے جب تم اس کام کو کرنا شروع کرتے ہو۔

﴿And you are not engaged in any affair, nor do you recite from it any part of the Quran, nor do you do any deed, but We are witnesses over you when you are engaged in it.﴾

The address in تَکُوْنُ is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the address in لاَ تَعْمَلُوْنَ is to all people. شَأنٍ means matter or state. A researcher has said that شان is applied to a great state and an exalted matter. Baydawi has written: (شان means intention) "I intended his like of intention (شَأنْتُ شَانَہٗ)." The pronoun in مِنْہُ refers to شان. The recitation of the Quran was a great achievement of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Alternatively, مِنْ is for the beginning of the point (ابتداء), meaning the recitation you make out of the greatness of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) station. In مِنْ قرآن, the من is explanatory (بیانیہ), or partitive (تبعیضیہ), or superfluous (زائد). Whatever you (ﷺ) recite, that is the Quran, or the part of the Quran you recite. وَلاَ تَعْمَلُوْنَ مِنْ عَمَلٍ: the first address was specifically to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because he was the leader of all humankind, so his great and magnificent deeds were mentioned; then all people were addressed and every small and large deed of theirs was mentioned. شھود means overseer, one who is aware. اِذْ تُفِیْضُوْنَ means when you begin that deed and enter into it. Some have said that افاضہ means doing a matter abundantly, so تُفِیْضُوْنَ came to mean "in abundance."

وما یعزب عن ربک من مثقال ذرۃ فی الارض ولا فی السمآہ ولا اصغر من ذلک ولا اکبر فی کتب مبین۔ اور آپ کے رب سے کوئی چیز ذرہ برابر بھی غائب نہیں، نہ زمین میں اور نہ آسمان میں، اور کوئی چیز ذرہ سے بھی چھوٹی یا بڑی ایسی نہیں کہ واضح کتاب (لوح محفوظ، اللہ کی علمی کتاب) میں نہ ہو۔

﴿Nor is hidden from your Lord the weight of an atom's particle in the earth or in the heaven, nor anything smaller than that nor greater, but it is in a clear Book.﴾

مَا یَعْزُبُ غائب نہیں ہے۔ مِنْ مِّثْقَالِ: مِنْ is superfluous. مثقال is a verbal noun meaning weight. ذَرَّۃٍ means a small ant or a particle of dust. By زمین و آسمان is meant the whole universe of possibility and the world of existence. The vision of common people with limited understanding can reach only these two, so only these two were mentioned. And since the condition of the people of the earth was in view, the earth was mentioned before the heaven. The purpose is that Allah's knowledge is all-encompassing, embracing the entire universe.

لاآ اَصْغَرَ وَلاآ اَکْبَرَالخ is an independent sentence. By کتاب is meant the Preserved Tablet (لوح محفوظ) or the record of deeds kept by the Noble Recording Angels (کرام کاتبین).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 62:

Be warned! The friends of Allah (on the Day when all people will be beset with the fear of calamity) will have no fear (of punishment), nor will they grieve (over the failure of any hope), meaning that every one of their hopes will be fulfilled.

The lexical meaning of "wilayah" (ولایت) and "tawalla" (تولی) is a direct and unmediated connection or union between two or more things. Figuratively, it denotes nearness, whether spatial, by lineage, religious, doctrinal, or in terms of friendship and support. In the Qamus it is stated: "Wali" (ولی) means nearness; "Wali" (ولی) is a form of the attributive noun, meaning one who has nearness, a friend, a helper.

Discussion

In a general sense, every person, indeed every thing, has a nearness to Allah whose modality cannot be known. Allah says: ﴿We are nearer to him than his jugular vein﴾. Because of this nearness, this universe takes on the garment of existence and comes into the sphere of being. Were it not for this nearness, no one could even smell the scent of existence. In terms of its essential reality, everything is nothingness; the origin of all is non-existence. Yet to special servants there is an additional nearness that is without modality; this nearness is love. In the world of similitude, the people of unveiling (ahl-e kashf) see this modality-less love in the form of physical nearness. The word "qurb" (قرب) is applied to both natural nearness and the nearness of love by way of verbal homonymy; the true reality of nearness differs in each case. The latter nearness has countless, unlimited degrees. There is a sacred hadith (Allah said): "My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts of worship until I love him. When I love him, I become his hearing with which he hears, and his sight with which he sees…" to the end of the hadith (meaning that at that time whatever deed he performs is, as it were, My deed). Narrated by al-Bukhari from Abu Hurairah.

The initial level of this nearness is attained through faith alone. Allah says: ﴿Allah is the Friend of those who believe﴾. The final, most complete level is the special portion of the prophets, whose chief is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The ranks of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continue to progress without any limit.

In the terminology of the Sufis, the least level to which the term "wali" (friend of Allah) can be applied is that of a person whose heart is ever immersed in the remembrance of Allah. He remains occupied morning and evening in glorifying Allah, and is saturated with the love of Allah. There is no room in him for the love of anyone else, whether father, son, brother, wife, or other relatives; he feels no love for them. If he loves anyone, it is only for the sake of Allah, and if he dislikes anyone, it is also for the sake of seeking the pleasure of his Master. He gives to someone only for Allah, and if he withholds, it is also for the sake of Allah's will. The mutual love of this group is for the sake of Allah. In the terminology of the Sufis, this quality is called "fana' al-qalb" (annihilation of the heart). The outward and inward being of the wali is adorned with taqwa. He keeps away from deeds and morals that are displeasing to Allah. He remains free from both hidden and manifest shirk, and even avoids that shirk which is more subtle than the sound of an ant's footstep. He is purified of pride, rancor, envy, greed and lust, and is adorned with noble morals and deeds. The Sufis call this station "fana' al-nafs" (annihilation of the self). The Sufis say that when a wali reaches this level, his Satan lays down his arms before him and becomes obedient. Towards the initial level of wilayah, Allah has...

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 63:

The words "those who believed" indicate that the friends of Allah (awliya' Allah) are those who have come to faith, meaning that the reality of faith has come into being within them. The seat of faith is the heart. The perfection of faith is that remembrance of Allah brings tranquility to the heart, that one is not heedless of the remembrance of Allah even for a moment, and that one's attention is not turned towards anything else. This points to the second level.

"And they used to be God-fearing": they refrain (from shirk and sins). That is, they observe the commands and prohibitions of Allah both outwardly and inwardly, in every respect.

Abu Dawud, through the narration of Hazrat Umar ibn al-Khattab, has recorded that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Among the servants of Allah there are some people who are neither prophets nor martyrs, yet on the Day of Judgment the prophets and martyrs will envy them because of their station of nearness. The Companions said: O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who are they? He said: Those who love one another for the sake of Allah alone. There are no kinship ties between them, nor any financial dealings (so that love arises from kinship or material greed). By Allah, their faces will be light, upon light. When others are in fear (of punishment), they will have no fear; when others are in grief, they will not grieve. Then he recited this verse: "Verily, the friends of Allah, no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve." Baghawi has also related this hadith in the same way through the narration of Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, and Bayhaqi has written the same in Shu'ab al-Iman.

It is narrated from Hazrat Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the meaning of the verse "Verily, the friends of Allah." He said: They are those who love one another for the sake of Allah. Ibn Mardawayh has also written the same through the narration of Hazrat Jabir.

Means of Attaining Wilayah

The attainment of the station of wilayah comes through the reflection of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whether the reflection of prophethood falls directly or through one intermediary or several intermediaries. Love for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) or his deputies, companionship with them, and obedience to them are necessary for attaining wilayah. The colour of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in heart, soul and body passes onto the heart, being and body of the wali because of these two qualities, and this is the "sibghat Allah" concerning which it was said: "The colour of Allah; and who is better in colour than Allah?" Abundant remembrance of Allah according to the Sunnah helps in receiving this reflection; it removes the rust from the heart and, by polishing the mirror of the heart, increases its capacity to reflect. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Everything has a polisher, and the polisher of the heart is the remembrance of Allah. Narrated by Bayhaqi.

From Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As: Imam Malik, Imam Ahmad and Bayhaqi related through the narration of Hazrat Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself say that Allah said: Those who love one another for My sake, sit together for My sake, and spend for My sake, upon them My love becomes obligatory.

Imam Ahmad, Tabarani and Hakim have also related this hadith through the narration of Hazrat Ubadah ibn al-Samit. In the Sahihayn, through the narration of Hazrat Ibn Mas'ud, it is reported that a man came into the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), what do you say about a person who loves a people but cannot reach their level (of deeds)? He said: A person will be counted among those whom he loves. Not being able to reach them means that his deeds could not be like the deeds of that people. In the Sahihayn, a similar hadith has come through the narration of Hazrat Anas.

Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman has written that Hazrat Abu Razin said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: Shall I tell you upon what the matter depends by which you will obtain the good of this world and the Hereafter? (The basis of good is this:) be constant in attending the gatherings of those who remember Allah, and when you are alone, keep your tongue moving with the remembrance of Allah as much as you can; and love and hate for the sake of Allah (that is, love and enmity for the sake of seeking Allah's pleasure, with no personal motive).

Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud have related through the narration of Hazrat Abu Dharr that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: The most beloved deed to Allah is that love and hatred be for the sake of Allah's pleasure.

Who Is the Beloved of Allah

A group among the awliya' also attains the rank of being beloved of Allah. Muslim, through the narration of Hazrat Abu Hurairah, has recorded that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: When Allah loves a servant, He summons Jibril and commands: I love so-and-so, so you also love him. Jibril then loves that servant, and then Jibril calls out in the heavens: Allah loves so-and-so, so you also love him. The inhabitants of heaven then love him. Then acceptance is granted to him among the people of the earth. And when Allah hates a servant, He summons Jibril and commands: I hate so-and-so, so you also hate him. Jibril then hates him, and then Jibril calls out among the inhabitants of heaven: Allah hates so-and-so, so you also hate him. They then hate him, and then hatred for him is created among the people of the earth.

Section

What are the signs of the awliya' of Allah?

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: Who are the awliya' of Allah? He said: Those whose sight reminds one of Allah (Baghawi). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said that Allah said: Among My servants, My awliya' are those whose remembrance is through My remembrance, and whose remembrance of Me is through their remembrance (Baghawi).

Hazrat Asma bint Yazid heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: Listen! Shall I not tell you who among you are the best people? The Companions said: O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), please do tell us. He said: Those whose sight reminds one of Allah (narrated by Ibn Majah).

Benefit: The essence of this is that the awliya' of Allah have closeness to Allah and a non-modal companionship; for this reason their company is, as it were, the company of Allah, their sight is a reminder of Allah, and their remembrance is a cause of the remembrance of Allah. Their example is like a mirror placed before the sun, which is lit up by the rays of the sun, and whatever is placed before that mirror is also illuminated by the mirror's reflection; indeed, if cotton is placed very close to that mirror, the cotton burns due to the mirror's nearness, while since the sun is distant, cotton does not burn in the sunlight. Another point is that Allah has placed in the awliya' a strong capacity for being influenced and influencing. Because of their closeness to Allah and non-modal affinity, the capacity of the awliya' to be influenced is stronger, and because of commonality of kind, species and personal resemblance, their capacity to influence other similar individuals, of the same kind, species and personality, is also strong. It is this relation of influence and being influenced that causes their presence to be a means of presence before Allah, and their being seen and their company to be a cause of the remembrance of Allah, provided that there is no denial in the heart of the one who sees or sits with them (deniers receive no benefit). And Allah does not guide the transgressing people: Allah does not guide those who step outside the bounds of faith and obedience.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said that Allah said: Whoever is hostile to My wali, I have declared war upon him (from My side). Narrated by Bukhari from Abu Hurairah.

Hazrat Hanzalah had said: O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when we are in your presence and you remind us of Hell and Paradise, it is as if we see Paradise and Hell with our own eyes; but when we leave your presence and become occupied with wives, children and disputes over lands, we forget much (of Paradise and Hell). He said: By the One in whose hand is my soul, if you remained continually in the state in which you are in my presence and during my admonition, the angels would shake hands with you on your beds and on your roads; but, Hanzalah, there is a time for everything (one time for being in my presence, one time for being absent). He said this three times. Narrated by Muslim.

Benefit: Ordinary people consider miraculous powers (karamat) and unveilings (kashf) a special sign of wilayah, but this is mistaken. Many awliya' are free of kashf and karamat, and sometimes, by way of istidraj, unusual events and hidden unveilings are found among people other than the awliya' as well. Therefore kashf and karamat are not the criterion of wilayah. If some awliya' happen to manifest kashf and karamat, one should not conclude from this that kashf and karamat are the criterion of wilayah. Allah addressed His noble Messenger (ﷺ) saying: "Say: I am only a man like you; it is revealed to me." In another place He addressed him: "Say: Had I known the unseen, I would have acquired much good, and harm would not have touched me." In another place He said: "Say: The signs are only with Allah."

The Sufis have said: Karamat is the menstruation of men; it is necessary to conceal it. A wali does not gain superiority over another wali through karamat; for this reason, those awliya' through whose hands karamat appeared more frequently felt regret over that act.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 64:

﴿For them is good news in the life of this world.﴾ This good news is the same that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave to the Companions in general and to some particular Companions in particular.

Tirmidhi, through the narration of Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf, and Ibn Majah, through the reference of Sa'id ibn Zayd, have reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Abu Bakr is in Paradise (i.e., he is among the people of Paradise), Umar is in Paradise, Uthman is in Paradise, Ali is in Paradise, Talhah is in Paradise, Zubayr is in Paradise, Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf is in Paradise, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas is in Paradise, Sa'id ibn Zayd is in Paradise, Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah is in Paradise."

Abu Dawud, through the narration of Abu Hurayrah, reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among my Ummah, the first to enter Paradise will be you, O Abu Bakr!" Tirmidhi, through the narration of Abu Hurayrah, reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first to emerge from the earth splitting open will be me, then Abu Bakr, then Umar." Tirmidhi, through the narration of Talhah ibn Ubaydullah, reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every Prophet has a companion, and my companion in Paradise will be Uthman."

Bukhari and Muslim, in the Sahihayn, through the narration of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Ali: "Your position with respect to me is the position Harun had with respect to Musa (i.e., the nearness of rank, lineage or love that Harun had from Musa is the nearness you have with me), except that there is no Prophet after me."

Imam Ahmad and Tirmidhi, through the narration of Zayd ibn Arqam, reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "For whomever I am the mawla (master, chief, friend), Ali is also his mawla."

Bukhari and Muslim in the Sahihayn, through the narration of Miswar ibn Makhramah, state that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Fatimah is a piece of me. Whoever angers her has angered me."

Tirmidhi, through the narration of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, reported: "Hasan and Husayn are the leaders of the youth of Paradise." He also said: "The best of the women of Paradise are Maryam bint Imran and Khadijah bint Khuwaylid." And he said: "The superiority of Aishah over women is like the superiority of thareed over (other) foods." He also said that Abdullah, that is Ibn Umar, is a righteous man (Bukhari and Muslim in the Sahihayn from Ibn Umar). About Abdullah ibn Salam he said that he is among the people of Paradise (agreed upon, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas). And he said: "None loves the Ansar except a believer, and none harbours enmity towards them except a hypocrite (i.e., love for the Ansar is a sign of faith and enmity towards them is a sign of hypocrisy). Whoever loves them, Allah will love him, and whoever harbours enmity towards them, Allah will be displeased with him." And he said: "How excellent a man is Usayd ibn Hudayr. How excellent a man is Thabit ibn Qays. How excellent a man is Mu'adh ibn Jabal. How excellent a man is Mu'adh ibn Amr ibn Jamuh."

And he said: "Paradise longs for three persons: Ali, Ammar, Salman." The Messenger (ﷺ) in this manner gave detailed good news to a great number of Companions.

Allah, giving good news to all the Companions, has said: ﴿And to each Allah has promised the best reward﴾. In another verse He also gave general good news, saying: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him...﴾ etc.

The Messenger (ﷺ) said: "Do not revile my Companions, for if any of you were to spend gold equal to (Mount) Uhud in the way of Allah, it would not reach one mudd or even half a mudd of what they spent." (Bukhari and Muslim in the Sahihayn, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.)

Razin reported through the narration of Umar that the Messenger (ﷺ) said: "My Companions are like stars; whichever of them you follow, you will be guided."

And he said: "The best people of my Ummah are those of my time, then those who come after them, and then those who come after them" (agreed upon, from Imran ibn Husayn).

After the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the worldly good news is that which Allah gives to His friends, through a dream or in a waking state, by revealing the world of similitude (alam-e-mithal). The "true dream" (ru'ya salihah) refers to this revelation of the world of similitude.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Apart from mubashshirat (good news), no part of prophethood remains" (i.e., after me, people will receive nothing from Allah's word, either directly or through angels, except good news; the door of prophethood has closed). The Companions asked: "What are mubashshirat?" He said: "True dreams." (Bukhari, from Abu Hurayrah.)

Hadrat Ubadah ibn al-Samit narrates: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to explain the verse ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world﴾. He said: (By "bushra" is meant) a true dream which is shown to a person (Baghawi).

Hadrat Abu Darda was asked about the meaning of ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world﴾, and he said: "Since I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the explanation of this verse, no one other than you has asked me about it. I had asked the Messenger (ﷺ), and he had said: 'Since this verse was revealed, no one other than you has asked about its meaning.' (Bushra) means a true dream which is shown to a believer. For them there is good news in worldly life, and in the Hereafter the good news will be Paradise" (Imam Ahmad and Sa'id ibn Mansur). This hadith has come through many chains.

By "true dreams" are meant not the dreams of ordinary people, but the dreams of friends of Allah and the righteous. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Dreams are of three kinds: (one) good news from Allah, (second) the speech of the self (i.e., mental imaginings or subconscious thoughts), (third) a frightening from Satan (i.e., terrifying, nonsensical dreams)." Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah reported this hadith through the narration of Abu Hurayrah, and Tirmidhi declared it sahih.

An objection: A dream, even if it is of friends of Allah and the righteous, does not produce certainty (whereas good news from Allah should produce certainty).

Answer: If a dream does not produce certainty, it certainly produces strong probability, and for good news, strong probability is sufficient.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) declared: "Out of forty-six parts of prophethood, one part is a true dream." This hadith is reported by Bukhari through the narration of Abu Sa'id, by Muslim through the narrations of Ibn Umar and Abu Hurayrah, and by Ahmad and Ibn Majah through the narration of Ibn Mas'ud. Ibn Majah has reported a similar hadith through the narration of Awf ibn Malik as well.

Imam Ahmad, through the narrations of Ibn Amr and Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Majah, through the narration of Ibn Umar, reported that a true dream is one of seventy parts of prophethood.

Ibn al-Najjar reported a saying of Ibn Umar that a true dream is one of twenty-five parts of prophethood.

The "bushra" refers to the general good news whose connection is with Paradise and reward. This good news is certainly given to all believers, but its manifestation will occur when one dies in faith, and whether one knows that one has died in faith or not.

According to some scholars, "bushra" means praise from people. Baghawi, through the narration of Abdullah ibn Samit, reported that Abu Dhar said: "O Messenger of Allah! A person does good deeds for himself, yet people come to love him." He said: "For the believer, this is worldly good news." In Muslim's narration, instead of "love him," the wording "they praise him" appears. Zuhri and Qatadah said: At the time of death, angels descend from Allah bearing good news; "bushra" means precisely this. Allah said: ﴿The angels descend upon them, saying: Do not fear and do not grieve, and receive the good news of Paradise﴾. In the narration of Ata, this is also the saying of Ibn Abbas.

"And in the Hereafter": that is, at the time the soul departs, the believer's soul is taken toward nearness to Allah, and the good news of Allah's pleasure is given; and on the Day of Judgment, when he rises from the grave, he will also be given good news.

Hadrat Ubadah ibn al-Samit narrates that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah also loves to meet him, and whoever dislikes meeting Allah, Allah also dislikes meeting him." Hadrat Aishah, or another wife, said: "O Messenger of Allah! We do not like death." He said: "That is not the meaning. Rather, when the believer's time of death comes, he is given the good news of Allah's pleasure and mercy, so he longs to meet Allah; and when the death of the disbeliever approaches, he is informed of Allah's punishment and retribution. Nothing is more hateful to him than the punishment that is coming before him, so he does not like to meet Allah, and Allah also dislikes meeting him." (Bukhari and Muslim in the Sahihayn.)

Hadrat Ibn Umar narrates that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Those who say La ilaha illa Allah will feel no fear at the time of death, nor in graves, nor at the time of rising from graves. It is as if I see before me the scene when, at the blast (sound of the trumpet), they (the believers) shake the dust from their heads, saying: 'Praise belongs to Allah, who has removed grief from us.'" (Tabarani.) Khatli, in Dibaj, has also related a marfu' saying of Ibn Abbas in the same manner.

La tabdila li-kalimati Allah: There is no alteration in the words of Allah. That is, His promises cannot be contrary.

Dhalika huwa al-fawz al-azim: That is, for believers to be given good news in both worlds is itself the great success. This sentence and the one before it are "parenthetical clauses" (jumla mu'taridah), by which the greatness and truth of the reward promised is expressed. For a clause to be parenthetical, it is not necessary that it appear between the beginning and end of a statement; the final part of a statement may be that which is connected to the beginning.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 65:

Let not their speech grieve you (آپ ان کی باتوں سے غمگین نہ ہوں). "Speech" here refers to the word of shirk, the denial (takdhib) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the threats to cause harm.

"Indeed, all might (al-'izzah) belongs to Allah" (ان العزۃ اللہ جمیعًا), because all power and dominance belong entirely to Allah (ساری طاقت اسی کو حاصل ہے); nothing is in anyone's control. Allah is dominant over all; He will help you and grant you success.

"He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing" (ھو السمیع العلیم). He (hears their words and knows their intentions). That is, He Himself will punish them.

Verily, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth belongs to Allah. Know well: those beings in the heavens and on the earth (angels, jinn and humans) are created by Allah, owned by Him, subjected to Him and His servants. And when those beings, who are the highest of all creation, are subject to Allah and worship Him, none of them is fit to be a lord. So how can a creature that is ignorant, lifeless and senseless be a partner or equal of Allah? Therefore:

﴿And those who call upon other than Allah as partners do not follow anything of the kind.﴾ Those who call upon others besides Allah do not follow a creature that is a partner of Allah.

﴿They follow nothing but assumption.﴾ They follow only their own conjecture. Those whom they have made partners in worship in their own imagination, they worship only them.

It is also possible that in ﴿ma yattabi'u﴾ the word "ma" is interrogative expressing denial, or that it is a relative pronoun (mawsulah), and that it is conjoined with ﴿man fi as-samawati﴾.

﴿And they are merely guessing.﴾ That is, in declaring these deities to be partners of Allah they tell lies, or this is merely their own fabrication. Wrongly, they are assigning these deities a share in divinity.

He it is who made the night for you that you may rest therein, [i.e., so that you may take repose at night from the fatigue you suffer from the labour of the day],

and the day to give light. [He made the day bright, so that by its light the things of the world become visible.]

Indeed in this there are signs for people who listen. [That is, the creation of such mighty things by Allah, which He made under the influence of His wisdom, contains within it signs that reveal the perfect power of Allah, His great favour and comprehensive wisdom, and establish that Allah alone deserves to be worshipped. But all these signs benefit only those people who listen to the Word of Allah and the admonition of those who guide, with the ears of reflection and lesson.]

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 68:

They said: "Allah has taken a son." That is, the polytheists claim that Allah has offspring; namely, that the angels are Allah's daughters.

Subhanahu (Glory be to Him, free of this slander). That is, He is exalted above becoming anyone's father. This phrase is both a declaration of His transcendence (tanzih) and an expression of astonishment at the speech of fools, that these people are saying something whose occurrence is impossible and whose very conception is impossible (that is, "Subhan Allah! What a grave thing they are saying").

Huwa al-Ghani: He is the One free of need; He has no need of anything. He has no requirement for anyone. Everything other than Him is contingent (mumkin). In His existence, the continuance of His existence, and all His states and attributes, everything is in need of Him. There is no affinity between the self-sufficient Allah and the needy contingent being. Then how could Allah have a child and any creature be His offspring? A child ought to be of the same kind as its father. Or, put another way, the need for offspring arises where the father is weak and wishes to gain strength through a son, or where he is poor and seeks financial help from a son, or where he lacks honour and a capable son becomes a source of honour for him, or where the father is mortal and wishes to preserve his lineage. In every case, a father's desire for a son is shaped by some purpose and need. Allah is free of every kind of need mentioned above; He is the Self-Sufficient and the Eternal.

Lahu ma fi as-samawati wa ma fi al-ard: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. That is, everything is His creation and possession. Then how could anything among them be Allah's offspring? (A child is neither the possession of its father nor his creation.)

In inna 'indakum min sultanin bihadha: You have no proof for this. That is, against the proof negating a son, there is no proof on your side.

Ataqulna 'ala Allahi ma la ta'lamun: Are you attributing to Allah something about which you have no knowledge (grounded in any evidence)?

In this sentence there is a rebuke to the polytheists for their ignorance and a warning that it is not proper to speak without evidence. For beliefs (aqa'id), certain and indubitable proof is required. Blindly following the speculative assumptions of others is in no way permissible.
Say, [O Muhammad (ﷺ)]: Indeed, those who fabricate lies against Allah will not succeed. They will neither be spared the Fire nor attain Paradise.

This passage is from Sayyid Qutb's commentary and is in Urdu, but the text here is a tafsir excerpt, so I'll translate it as it stands.

"Matā'un fid-dunyā" (a brief enjoyment in this world): this worldly life is a little pleasure. That is, this fabrication will become a cause of enjoying some pleasure in the world. In this way, they will be able to maintain their leadership while in a state of disbelief. Or, their worldly life is a contemptible enjoyment.

"Thumma ilaynā marji'uhum, thumma nudhīquhumu al-'adhāba ash-shadīda bimā kānū yakfurūn" (Then to Us is their return; then We shall make them taste the severe punishment because of their disbelief): Then (after death) their return will be to Us alone, then We will make them taste the severe punishment in recompense for their disbelief.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 71:

وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ نُوحٍ: And (O Muhammad (ﷺ)!) recite to them (the people of Makkah) the account of Nuh. That is, recite before them the story of Hazrat Nuh with his people.

إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ: Remember when Nuh said to his people. According to al-Baghawi, the people of Nuh were from the lineage of Qabil, but this is not possible, because Hazrat Nuh was from the lineage of Shayth (Seth), not from the lineage of Qabil. And since the people are attributed to Hazrat Nuh, it is proven that the people of Nuh were from the lineage of Hazrat Shayth.

يَا قَوْمِ إِن كَانَ كَبُرَ عَلَيْكُم مَّقَامِي: O my people! If my staying among you has become burdensome to you. That is, if my long residence among you, or my remaining steadfast in the call, has become distasteful to you.

وَتَذْكِيرِي بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ: And my admonition by the signs of Allah (and my reminding you of the commands of Allah has become burdensome and heavy to you).

فَعَلَى اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ: Then upon Allah I have relied (I rely upon Allah alone).

فَأَجْمِعُوا أَمْرَكُمْ وَشُرَكَاءَكُمْ: So resolve upon your plan, along with your associates (whom you imagine as partners), to harm me.

أَجْمَعَ الْأَمْرَ: He resolved upon the matter, made a firm decision. That is, you and your supposed partners should firmly resolve to kill me or inflict harm upon me (as al-Zajjaj said). Or, there is an omitted genitive before "shuraka'akum", meaning: set right your affair and the affair of your partners. Or the meaning is: resolve firmly upon your affair and also call your (supposed) partners.

ثُمَّ لَا يَكُنْ أَمْرُكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ غُمَّةً: Then let your plan not be a source of distress in your hearts. Ghummah means concealed, hidden. Ghamma-hu means he concealed it. That is, your plan should not remain hidden; strive to achieve your aim in a completely open manner. Or the meaning is: when you have destroyed me and been freed from the burden of my day and night admonition and preaching, your condition should not remain concealed from you.

ثُمَّ اقْضُوا إِلَيَّ: Then carry out whatever you intend to do to me.

وَلَا تُنظِرُونِ: And do not give me any respite at all. In this speech of Hazrat Nuh, the imperative is used to express incapacitation (that is, you cannot actually do it; if you can, then do it, why are you waiting?). The purpose of quoting this speech is to show that Hazrat Nuh's trust in his Lord was extremely firm. He relied on Allah's help and was not afraid of any secret plan of his people. He was certain that his people and their deities could do nothing: neither benefit nor harm lay in their power.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 72:

﴿Then if you turn away, I have not asked you for any reward.﴾ (Meaning: even if you still persist in turning away, know that I do not seek any compensation from you.)

The consequence (jaza') has been omitted, and the reason for the consequence has been mentioned in its place. The explanatory meaning is as follows: if you still turn away from my admonition and do not accept my words, you will be destroyed, or Allah will punish you, because there is no reasonable cause for your turning away. Nothing prevents you from accepting the truth. I have no personal aim in this preaching and admonition. I do not ask you for a reward for this call, so that you cannot pay the reward and therefore turn away, or so that you may accuse me (of the charge of seeking worldly gain). Or the meaning is that if you turn away, you will harm yourselves, and I will suffer no harm. I do not seek a reward from you, so that your turning away would deprive me of a reward. It is you who will be harmed; you yourselves will be deprived of guidance.

﴿My reward is only with Allah.﴾ (Meaning: my reward for this call and admonition rests only with Allah.) That is, I have no connection to any reward from you. Whether you believe or not, Allah will give the reward for my deeds.

From this statement it is indirectly deduced that it is not permissible to take payment for teaching the Qur'an and similar things (teaching the Qur'an and hadith is also propagation of the religion, and taking payment from those to whom the religion is propagated appears, on the apparent meaning of this verse, to be impermissible).

﴿And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims.﴾ (Meaning: I have been commanded to obey Allah's command and to believe.)

I should also follow the commands of Allah in my actions, call people to them as well, and I have carried out and am carrying out this command.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 73:

Then they denied him, and the people of Noah persisted in denial, even after the truth had become clear, out of mere obstinacy and stubbornness.

So We saved him and those with him in the ark. They were eighty people in all.

And We made them successors, and We drowned those who had denied Our signs. So (O Prophet) see how the end of those who had been warned turned out.

That is, those people to whom the messengers had given warning of the punishment for disobedience to Allah, and who did not believe, see how they were destroyed.

In this sentence there is a message of consolation for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and a warning of a grievous punishment for those who deny.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 74:

Then after him We sent messengers to their peoples, (many messengers, in various numbers) ... that is, We sent each messenger to his own people.

So they brought them clear proofs, but they were not such as to believe in what they had earlier denied. Thus do We seal the hearts of transgressors.

That is, just as We sealed the hearts of the peoples of Noah and of the nations of the messengers who came after him (We left them without help), so too We seal the hearts of those among your ummah who transgress the command of God. And since they are themselves immersed in misguidance and do not abandon their base desires, so We too leave them without help.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 10, verse 75:

Then after them We sent Musa (bin Imran) and his brother Harun to Fir'awn and his chiefs with Our signs, but they showed arrogance, for they were a criminal people. (Note: the translation of the Quranic verses below is given as they stand in the passage.)

Quranic verse: ﴿Then after them We sent Musa and Harun to Fir'awn and his chiefs with Our signs.﴾ Since the next verse describes the rebellion of Fir'awn's people, the word "chiefs" has been mentioned here alongside Fir'awn.

﴿So they behaved arrogantly, and they were a criminal people.﴾ That is, they regarded it as beneath them to accept the word of Musa and Harun, and they became proud (and therefore did not follow). They were accustomed to crime, habituated to it, and so they regarded the message of prophethood as contemptible and dared to reject it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verse 76:

﴿Then when the truth came to them from Us, they said: "Indeed, this is clear magic."﴾ That is, when the religion of truth reached Pharaoh and his chiefs, and they understood its truth through clear and undeniable miracles, they still did not accept it, out of obstinacy and rebellion. They declared the miracles presented by Musa to be clear magic, and they called Musa an accomplished magician.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 10, verse 77:

قال موسیٰ اتقولون للحق لما جاء کم اسحر ھذا موسیٰ نے کہا : کیا حق جب تمہارے پاس آگیا تو تم اس کو سحر کہتے ہو۔ کیا یہ جادو ہے ؟

Musa (AS) said: "Do you say this of the truth when it has come to you? Is this magic?"

(Translation note: the Urdu rendering of the verse is kept as it stands above, with the Arabic and Urdu retained exactly as in the source.)

Yaʿni Hazrat Musa ne batoor ujab-o-inkar kaha ke jis amr ki sadaqat-o-haqqaniyat Allah ki taraf se hai, tum is ko sihr kehte ho? Sihr ki to koi haqiqat nahin hoti, woh to sirf faraib-kari hota hai. Yaqooloon ka maf'ool mahzoof hai. Asihrun maf'ool nahin hai, yeh alag jumla hai.

Wa la yuflihu's-sahirun. Aur jadugar kamyab nahin hote. Yeh jumla Hazrat Musa ke kalam ka tatimma hai, yaʿni yeh jadu nahin hai. Agar jadu hota to nabood ho jata aur jadugaron ke jadu ko tabah na kar sakta. Ya yeh fiqra Firaunion ke qaul (sihr hadha) ka takmila aur juz hai. Goya Firaunion ne kaha tha ke Musa! Kya tum jadu ka mazahira kar ke kamyabi hasil karna chahte ho? Jadugar kabhi kamyab nahin hote.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verses 78–80:

Pharaoh said: "Musa! Have you come to us so that you may turn us away from that (religion) upon which we found our fathers, and so that greatness in the land may belong to you two? We will never believe you."

Qatadah said: "Turn us away" (تلفتنا) means: turn us away from idol-worship, or from the worship of Pharaoh, which is the purpose for which you have come.

"Kibriya'" (greatness) means government and supreme authority. Worldly arrogance inevitably arises in kings, and for this reason kingship itself came to be called arrogance.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 10, verses 81–82:

﴿Then when they had cast, Moses said: "What you have brought is magic. Surely Allah will bring it to nothing. Indeed Allah does not set right the work of the corrupters."﴾

Verse 81 (Urdu commentary): When the magicians threw down their ropes and staffs, Moses said: "You have brought only magic." That is, what you have produced is sorcery and nothing more.

Verse 82 (Urdu commentary): "Surely Allah will bring it to nothing," that is, Allah will nullify it and expose that it has no reality.

"Indeed Allah does not set right the work of the corrupters," that is, Allah does not keep in place nor give strength to the deeds of those who spread corruption. From this verse it is established that magic has no reality; it is merely deception and the creation of mischief.
